cnd9:1.1: I ask you, Blessed One, tell me this,
cnd9:2.1: I ask you, Blessed One, tell me this.
cnd9:2.3: a question to illuminate the unseen, a question to compare with the seen, a question to cut off doubt …
cnd9:2.6: I ask you: I ask you, I beg you, I urge you, I entreat you; tell me—

cnd9:3.3: Venerable: this is an endearing word, a respectful word, a term of address showing reverence and deference, namely, venerable.

cnd9:4.1: I long for your words, great seer: I long for, I intensely long for, I wish for, I accept, I aspire to, I yearn for, I hanker for your word, speech, teaching, instruction, and counsel.
cnd9:4.3: Because he sought, searched for, and looked for the great aggregate of ethics, he is a great seer …

cnd9:6.3: the training in higher ethics, the training in higher mind, the training in higher wisdom …
cnd9:6.5: For my own extinguishment: for the extinguishing of one’s own greed,
cnd9:6.10: for the stilling, calming, settling, quenching, relinquishing, and subsiding of all unskillful choices, one should train in higher ethics, one should train in higher mind, one should train in higher wisdom.
cnd9:6.26: one should practice, practice fully, and take up and follow—

cnd9:15.4: Release me, Sakyan, from my indecisions.
cnd9:16.3: gods by convention, gods by rebirth, gods by purification.
cnd9:16.5: Gods by convention are said to be kings, princes, and queens.
cnd9:16.8: Gods by rebirth are said to be the gods of the Four Great Kings, the gods of the Thirty-Three, the gods of Yama, the Joyful gods, the gods who love to create, the gods who control what is created by others, the gods of Brahmā’s host, and the gods higher than them.
cnd9:16.11: Gods by purification are said to be the disciples of the Realized One who are perfected ones with defilements ended, and the independent Buddhas.
cnd9:16.13: The Blessed One is a god, a super-god, a god of gods, for the gods by convention, the gods by rebirth, and the gods by purification; a lion of lions, an elephant of elephants, a leader of leaders of groups, a sage of sages, a king of kings.
cnd9:16.14: I see in the world of gods and humans: in the human world I see a god, I see a super-god, I see a god of gods; I look upon, I observe, I contemplate, I examine—
cnd9:17.2: Having nothing: the possession of greed, the possession of hate, the possession of delusion, the possession of conceit, the possession of views, the possession of corruptions, the possession of misconduct; those possessions have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, unable to arise in the future. So the Buddha has nothing.
cnd9:17.3: Brahmin: the Blessed One is a brahmin because he has barred out seven things—
cnd9:17.4: substantialist view is barred out, doubt is barred out, misapprehension of precepts and observances is barred out, greed is barred out, hate is barred out, delusion is barred out, conceit is barred out; for him, bad, unskillful qualities that are corrupting, leading to future lives, troublesome, ripening in suffering, and leading to future rebirth, old age, and death are barred out.
cnd9:19.1: Traveling: living, dwelling, moving, proceeding, maintaining, sustaining, and keeping going—
cnd9:20.3: I bow: I bow with the body, or I bow with speech, or I bow with the mind; I bow by practicing in line with the meaning, or I bow by practicing in line with the teaching; I honor, I show respect, I esteem, I revere.
cnd9:20.4: All-seer: the all-seeing eye is said to be the knowledge of omniscience.
cnd9:20.5: The Blessed One is endowed, fully endowed, equipped, fully equipped, provided, fully provided, and possessed of the knowledge of omniscience.
cnd9:23.1: Release me, Sakyan, from my indecisions.
cnd9:23.2: Sakyan: the Blessed One is a Sakyan; one who went forth from the Sakyan clan is also a Sakyan.
cnd9:23.3: Or else, one who is rich, with great wealth and property, is also a Sakyan.
cnd9:23.5: The wealth of faith, the wealth of ethics, the wealth of conscience, the wealth of prudence, the wealth of learning, the wealth of generosity, the wealth of wisdom, the wealth of mindfulness meditation, the wealth of right efforts, the wealth of the bases of psychic power, the wealth of the faculties, the wealth of the powers, the wealth of the awakening factors, the wealth of the path, the wealth of the fruit, the wealth of extinguishment.
cnd9:23.6: With these many kinds of jewels of wealth, one who is rich, with great wealth and property, is also a Sakyan.
cnd9:23.7: Or else, one who is capable, powerful, competent, heroic, brave, valiant, fearless, unshaken, unafraid, not fleeing, who has given up fear and terror, with goosebumps gone, is also a Sakyan.
cnd9:23.9: Doubt about suffering, doubt about the origin of suffering, doubt about the cessation of suffering, doubt about the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering, doubt about the past, doubt about the future, doubt about the past and the future, doubt about things that arise dependently, in terms of specific conditionality.
cnd9:23.10: Any such doubt: doubting, the state of doubting, wavering, uncertainty, hesitation, being in two minds, standing at a fork in the road, perplexity, taking sides without certainty, groping, groping around, not diving in, the trembling of the mind, mental scratching.
cnd9:23.11: Release me, Sakyan, from my indecisions: free me, release me, liberate me, completely liberate me, pull me out, pull me right out, lift me out, from the dart of indecision—
cnd9:26.1: I am not able to release: I am not able to free you, to release you, to liberate you, to completely liberate you, to pull you out, to pull you right out, to lift you out, or to lift you right out of the dart of indecision.
cnd9:26.3: Or else, I do not strive, I do not exert myself, I do not endeavor, I do not try, I do not make an effort, I do not make a vigorous effort, I do not show strength, I am not resolute, I do not show energy, I do not give rise to enthusiasm, I do not generate it, I do not bring it about, I do not bring it fully about for a person who is faithless, unenthusiastic, lazy, of poor energy, and who does not practice in line with the teaching of the Dhamma.
cnd9:26.6: If they were to be freed, they would be freed by their own strength, power, energy, and effort, by their own human strength, human power, human energy, and human effort, themselves practicing the right practice, the conforming practice, the non-opposing practice, the practice in accordance with the meaning, the practice in line with the teaching.
cnd9:27.2: “Cunda, it is quite impossible that someone who is themself sunk in the mud will pull out another who is sunk in the mud.
cnd9:27.3: Cunda, it is quite impossible that someone who is themself untamed, undisciplined, and not fully extinguished will tame, discipline, and fully extinguish another.”
cnd9:31.2: “In the same way, brahmin, extinguishment is present, the path leading to extinguishment is present, and I am present to encourage them; and yet, when my disciples are advised and instructed by me like this, some achieve the ultimate goal, extinguishment, while some do not achieve it.
cnd9:32.1: Anyone indecisive in the world, Dhotaka: an indecisive person, one with doubt, with rigidity, with vacillation, with uncertainty.
cnd9:32.2: Anyone: any aristocrat, brahmin, merchant, or worker; any householder or renunciate; any god or human.
cnd9:32.3: In the world: in the world of the lower realms … in the world of the sense fields—
cnd9:33.1: When you understand the best of teachings: the best teaching is said to be the deathless, extinguishment.
cnd9:33.2: That is the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
cnd9:33.3: Best: the foremost, best, finest, chief, highest, and most excellent teaching; understanding, knowing, comprehending, and penetrating it—
cnd9:34.1: You will cross this flood: in this way you might cross, cross over, cross beyond, completely get past, and go beyond the flood of sensuality, the flood of continued existence, the flood of views, and the flood of ignorance—
cnd9:37.1: Teach me, brahmin, out of compassion: teach me, brahmin, support me, brahmin, have sympathy for me, brahmin—
cnd9:37.3: Out of compassion: feeling compassion, feeling tenderness, protecting, supporting, and having sympathy—
cnd9:38.1: The principle of seclusion, so that I may understand: the principle of seclusion is said to be the deathless, extinguishment.
cnd9:38.2: That is the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
cnd9:38.3: So that I may understand: so that I might know, comprehend, understand, thoroughly understand, penetrate, attain, touch, and realize—
cnd9:39.1: As unobstructed as space itself: as space does not get stuck, does not grasp, is not bound, is not hindered, so too, not getting stuck, not grasping, not being bound, not being hindered—
cnd9:39.3: As space is not colored by lac, turmeric, indigo, or madder, so too, not lusting, not hating, not being deluded, not being defiled—
cnd9:39.5: As space does not become angry, does not become ill-willed, does not shrink back, is not struck, so too, not becoming angry, not becoming ill-willed, not shrinking back, not being struck, not being obstructed—

cnd9:45.7: Or else, apparent in the present, immediate, inviting inspection, relevant, to be personally experienced by the sensible; in this way too—

cnd9:59.4: For the sake of rebirth after rebirth: for the sake of one existence after another, for the sake of kamma-existence, for the sake of renewed existence, for the sake of sensual existence; for the sake of kamma-existence, sensual existence, renewed existence, and form existence; for the sake of kamma-existence, form existence, renewed existence, and formless existence; for the sake of kamma-existence, formless existence, renewed existence, and renewed existence again and again, destinations again and again, reappearance again and again, relinking again and again, and the generation of an individual existence again and again, do not produce craving: do not give rise to it, do not generate it, do not bring it about, do not bring it fully about; give it up, dispel it, eliminate it, and bring it to an end—
